title: Inside the battery box: a cross-technology assessment of PFAS uses, functions, and substitution potential
content: Understanding where and why per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are used in batteries is essential for evaluating their substitution potential, yet detailed information across battery technologies is scarce. We analyzed more than 5600 submissions to the Annex XV public consultation on the proposed universal PFAS restriction in the European Union and extracted information reporting use, associated substance(s), and stated function(s) of PFASs in batteries. 341 records were compiled into a database using our structured Battery Use & Function Framework that incorporates the Functional Substitution Framework. Among these records, 78 contained sufficient information to qualify as a potential PFAS use and were organized into 36 potential PFAS uses, accounting for overlaps. Each potential PFAS use was evaluated using supporting evidence from previous use-mapping studies, input from battery stakeholders, teardown-analysis studies, and other targeted academic literature. Across all lines of evidence, two PFAS uses in batteries were contradicted, indicating already large-scale availability of PFAS-free alternatives, while 16 PFAS uses were confirmed, primarily in cathode components across several battery technologies and chemistries. PFAS-free alternatives were identified for 13 PFAS uses across battery applications, with an additional five uses showing PFAS-free options for certain applications within the broader use category. The findings indicate that few technical barriers remain for substituting PFASs in most battery components. Our mapping provides a detailed foundation for future alternatives assessments, supports essential-use evaluations, and highlights opportunities and challenges relevant to monitoring and recycling.
